name: Should I hire a handyman or a general contractor for property maintenance?

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a handyman or a general contractor for property maintenance?

acceptedAnswer.text: For basic cosmetic touch-ups, hiring a specialized handyman is often sufficient. However, if your maintenance checklist involves coordinated work across drywall, tile, finish carpentry, and framing, working with a general finish contractor is usually more efficient. At HH Remodeling, owner Abraham Becerra leads the interior carpentry, drywall, and tile crew directly while coordinating specialized sub-trades for required plumbing or electrical work. This single point of contact prevents scheduling conflicts and ensures consistent craftsmanship across all repairs.
acceptedAnswer.description: A handyman suits single cosmetic tasks, but a general finish contractor provides a single point of contact for complex, multi-trade repairs involving framing, tile, and drywall.
